degenerate_cells.why_this_matters: A cell where no replicate produced a violating quadruple cannot calibrate anything: any positive observation is significant at the floor there. Knowing which regions of parameter space are degenerate BEFORE running an experiment is the single most useful thing this table buys, and is exactly what was missing when the topology and breakpoint experiments reported counts against empty nulls.

design.null_populations: clonal descent, no reticulation, at each grid point; relaxed clock where spread > 0
design.statistic: the maximum quartet margin, exhaustive over every quadruple -- the same floor `real-data` computes

experiment: the null's parameter space, swept, so the floor can be predicted rather than simulated per query
no_bisection: `mu` is swept directly and the ACHIEVED mean p-distance recorded, rather than tuning `mu` to hit a target divergence. The achieved divergence is the covariate a surrogate wants, and this removes the 40-step bisection from every cell.
what_is_predicted_and_what_is_not: Only the FLOOR would ever be predicted. The certificate's margin stays an exact integer comparison the kernel can check, so a wrong surrogate costs power or wastes a query -- never correctness. That is the condition for a fitted model to be admissible here at all.
why: Phase 3 of the plan -- the margin's null distribution -- is the oldest open item here, and no analytic sampling distribution of the four-point margin exists in the literature either. Every calibrated answer in this programme currently costs a matched simulation, and two experiments this session reported counts from nulls that could not vary because there was no cheap way to know in advance where the null is degenerate. This is the table a surrogate is fitted to.
